element.description: Use this wording for element-of-leverage pages where completion means merged delegated output.

jobToBeDone.title: Complete and Merge a Coding Task with Asynchronous use of an Agent
jobToBeDone.body: Developers assign issues to Copilot, which creates pull requests. Humans review and merge.

whatCountsAsCompletion.title: A Copilot-authored PR that gets merged
whatCountsAsCompletion.body: Valid = PR was reviewed and merged by a human reviewer. Failed/flawed = PR closed or abandoned without a merge.

jobClass.title: Value-creating
jobClass.body: Valid completions represent an intentional valuable result.

efficiency.description: Use this wording for efficiency pages where the question is how much human-equivalent value the coding agent creates relative to the hours and sessions engaged.

jobToBeDone.title: Complete and Merge a Coding Task with Asynchronous use of an Agent
jobToBeDone.body: Developers delegate implementation work to the coding agent, which creates pull requests that humans review, guide, and merge.

whatCountsAsCompletion.title: A Copilot-authored PR that gets merged
whatCountsAsCompletion.body: Valid = PR was reviewed and merged by a human reviewer. Failed/flawed = PR closed or abandoned without a merge.

jobClass.title: Value-creating
jobClass.body: Valid completions represent an intentional valuable result.

howEfficiencyImproves.title: Asynchronous GitHub Copilot Sessions complete Coding Tasks autonomously.
howEfficiencyImproves.body: Efficiency can show up if a completion 1) consumes fewer dev-hours, 2) encounters less risk, 3) is larger in size, scope, or difficulty, and/or 4) consumes fewer dollars than otherwise would have been required without Copilot.

estimatesAndAssumptions.title: Conversion factors translate merged agent activity into saved dev-hours
estimatesAndAssumptions.body: The hours spent is modeled as a percentage of Session Duration minutes and other Session Characteristics, which can be configured (reflecting an expectation that dev hours spent using Agents is growing as agent workload grows). Copilot Agent Session logs and statistics provide various measures of Agent session duration, costs, and failures.

indicatorsOfProgress.title: Increases in Sessions per day and improving Session characteristics, like Yield, indicate that average AI benefits from Agent Usage are increasing.
indicatorsOfProgress.body: When the modeled time savings based on multiple indicators agree, we have increasing confidence in the calculated average Leverage.
